findings: The existing keepalive saturation fix b026ca03 was already deployed. Its Chromium regression tests passed before this change.
The old queue discarded retryable network/HTTP failures on the sixth attempt, even though the server had not acknowledged the record.
A failing head row blocked later chat records; its waiting render receipt blocked unrelated receipts.
Queue writes silently removed old records above 80 chat rows or 120 render receipts.
reproduction: All five initial queue regression tests failed against config-before.js; all passed after the fix. Two additional timeout/concurrency tests also passed.
changes: Retain retryable failures with per-record retry timestamps and a 15-second to 120-second backoff; report delayed delivery once at attempt six.
Send ready records and independent receipts while failed records wait. Report and remove non-retryable payload errors.
Retain complete pending queues instead of slicing away unacknowledged records.
Resume flushing on pageshow and visible-tab restoration as well as online/load.
Preserve clientMsgId across retries and reloads; strip local retry metadata from transmitted payloads.
Advance assetVersion to 2.9.304 and service-worker cache to cupid-v3.3.223 without changing the displayed version.

validation.browserRecovery: HTTP 500 repeated six times preserves both turn rows; reload with restored service drains chat and render-ack queues with the original IDs.
validation.visualMethod: Chromium, fixed desktop/mobile viewports, local assets and mocked external requests; before/after config interception, screenshots with animations disabled. Software rendering removes a one-channel, one-pixel GPU edge fluctuation. All four final screenshot pairs are byte-identical.

limitations: The reproduction establishes code-path failures; it does not prove how many production users lost records.
Already discarded records cannot be restored by this change. Pending records can retry on a later visit.
Durability still depends on browser storage availability. The existing storage adapter can use memory when native storage is unavailable or full.
Non-retryable errors remain explicitly reported and removed. Route telemetry has its existing independent policy.
